Readable labels of variables

Source: R/labels.R
label_get.Rd

label_get() looks variable names up in a named vector of labels and falls back to the raw name. label_expand() builds labels of derived variables from a dictionary of root names: the visit suffix is removed first, then the prefixes one by one, so that DELTA_LOG_NFL becomes "Delta log(NfL)" and BIN_IL6_V0 becomes "IL-6 (high) V0".

Usage

label_get(var, labels = NULL)

label_expand(
  vars,
  base_labels,
  visit_map = c(V0 = "V0", V3 = "V3"),
  prefix_map = c(LOG = "log(%s)", LOG10 = "log10(%s)", LOG1P = "log(1+%s)", BC =
    "Box-Cox(%s)", SQRT = "√%s", BIN = NA, DELTA = "Δ %s", Z = "%s (z)"),
  bin_format = "%s (high)",
  bin_format_root = NULL
)

Arguments

var, vars

Character vector of variable names.

labels

Named character vector name -> label, or NULL.

base_labels

Named character vector of labels of the root names.

visit_map

Named vector suffix -> text appended to the label.

prefix_map

Named vector prefix -> sprintf() format. The BIN entry, when NA, is replaced by bin_format.

bin_format

Format of the categorised variables (BIN_ prefix), e.g. "%s (high)" for a median split or "%s (tertiles)".

bin_format_root

Optional named vector root -> format overriding bin_format for some roots (e.g. from lodestar::cut_label_formats()).

Value

label_get(): an unnamed character vector of labels. label_expand(): a character vector named by vars.

Examples

labs <- c(NFL = "NfL", IL6 = "IL-6")
label_get(c("NFL", "AGE"), labs)
#> [1] "NfL" "AGE"
label_expand(c("NFL_V0", "LOG_NFL_V3", "DELTA_LOG_NFL", "BIN_IL6_V0"), labs)
#>           NFL_V0       LOG_NFL_V3    DELTA_LOG_NFL       BIN_IL6_V0 
#>         "NfL V0"    "log(NfL) V3"     "Δ log(NfL)" "IL-6 (high) V0"
